### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4d36e6586f65ae2d11a6f14a506615020eb64bab` — the merge of head `2055ce2324552f66a7654791d750177a9859837d` into base `ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4d36e6586f65ae2d11a6f14a506615020eb64bab && git checkout 4d36e6586f65ae2d11a6f14a506615020eb64bab
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f 2055ce2324552f66a7654791d750177a9859837d && git checkout -B drift-repro ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f && git merge --no-ff 2055ce2324552f66a7654791d750177a9859837d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2055ce2324552f66a7654791d750177a9859837d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-app-publish-gate.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-list-projection-parity.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/meta-read-doors-live.dogfood.test.ts + packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts (the REST list door: `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` over `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.list`, `metaTypeSingular`, the hand-off to `createMetaListAnswer`, the `handleRouteError` catch), packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts (the dispatcher's one-segment list branch: `metaQueryArityRefusal('list')`, `pluralToSingular`, `answerMetaList` and its `errorFromThrown` catch), packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts (`readDispatchQuery`), packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts (`readQuery`), packages/rest/src/query-multiplicity.ts (`repeatedQueryParamMessage`), packages/rest/src/error-response.ts (`handleRouteError`), packages/rest/src/index.ts (the export list), packages/runtime/src/endpoint-executor.ts (the other `query.id` reader, a different door), .changeset/28930-bracketed-app-id-refused.md (read for ②), PR #28602's changeset and its PASS record 6555574011, PR #28850's file list and its hunks on the dogfood file. Inputs: card #28930 body and its three comments (triage 6569547911, claim 6569718113, os-dev-report 6570620675), PR #29046 body, file list and net diff against the merge-base `135054ebaa7fb4f1282714d6856a0a6a032a81fe`, and the 54 check-runs on this head. The merge-base and the branch were read with `git show` on fetched refs; nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated here.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each read against the cited code on the merge-base and on the head:

1. **`GET /meta/app` and `GET /meta/apps` with any query key that opens `id[` (`?id[]=NAME`, `?id[0]=NAME`, `?id[name]=NAME`): 200 with the caller's whole visible list → 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, no list, on both transports.** Right. Both adapters build the query with `Object.fromEntries` over `c.req.queries()` and parse no brackets (`readQuery` in `plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`, `readDispatchQuery` in `adapters/hono/src/index.ts`), so the key reaches the door spelled `id[]`. The list door declares no closed set (`META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS` docblock: recognition "never applies" to `list`), and its arity table names `id`, not `id[]`, so neither entry gate catches the key; on the merge-base step 3 of `createMetaListAnswer` read `query?.id` only, and the key fell through to the unfiltered list, which is the card's reproduction. On the head, step 3 asks `refuseBracketedAppIdFilter(query)` first, keyed on the folded `metaType === 'app'` (`metaTypeSingular` on the REST route, `pluralToSingular` in the dispatcher), so `apps` is covered and the plural is pinned. The throw carries `status = 400`, `code = 'VALIDATION_ERROR'` on an `Error`, the exact shape #28548's `refuseEmptyListFilter` throws; the REST route catches into `handleRouteError` and the dispatcher's `answerMetaList` into `deps.errorFromThrown(e, 500)`, the two catches PASS record 6555574011 already traced to the wire. The rest unit drives the real `GET /api/v1/meta/:type` handler and asserts `statusCode 400`, `body.code`, no `items` and no bare array; the parity row A asserts the same triple on `RestServer`; the dogfood pins it over HTTP on the booted Hono stack as admin and as a member.
2. **The refusal's sentence is one spelling for every bracketed key, in #28548's frame, and the two existing messages are byte-identical.** Right. `refuseEmptyListFilter` now delegates to `throwListFilterRefusal(param, param, names, lists, 'got ""', 'an empty NAMES name')`; expanding that builder reproduces the merge-base literal word for word for both `id`/`app` and `object`/`object`, so #28548's two answers do not move. The bracketed arm calls the same builder with the key as sent, so `id[]`, `id[0]` and `id[name]` differ only in the quoted key, which is what "one spelling, same words" means for a refusal that must name the spelling it refuses.
3. **A bracketed key beside a plain `?id=` is refused too.** Right. The bracket check runs before `appIdFilter` is read, so `{ id: 'crm', 'id[]': 'account' }` is 400 and never narrows to `crm`; pinned in the rest unit. A bracketed key supplied twice (`?id[]=a&id[]=b`) arrives as an array under `id[]`, which the arity table does not name, so the bracket refusal answers it with the same sentence: one answer for every bracketed shape.
4. **The refusal sits after the per-caller gate (step 2) and is caller-invariant.** Right. It reads only the query's keys, names only the key and a fixed sentence, and the rest unit runs it for `studio.access`, `manage_users` and no permission; the dogfood runs it for the admin and the `client_liaison` member. A caller who may see nothing learns nothing from it.
5. **Everything else is unchanged.** Right, read in the diff: `?id=NAME` narrows as before (`showcase_app` one app, `setup` on a stack without it an empty list); an absent `id` is `undefined` and takes no new branch; the empty `?id=` and the repeated `id` keep their 400s (the arity refusal at the door entry is untouched on both transports); the guard is keyed on `app`, so a bracketed `id` key on any other type stays unread, as `?id=` is there (the rest control on `view`, and the census's 2 probes × 26 type cells on both transports); `ids[`, `ID[` and the like do not match `startsWith('id[')`, consistent with `ids=` and `ID=` never being read; a non-object query returns early.
6. **Public surface: nothing added.** Right. `refuseBracketedAppIdFilter` and `throwListFilterRefusal` are module-private; the diff does not touch `packages/rest/src/index.ts`; no new error code, status, answer member or export. The only published change is the accept set of one door shrinking.
7. **"Does the seam serve other `/meta/:type` list doors?" The dev's answer, `/meta/app` only, is right.** On the head the sole `query.id` read on any `/meta` door is step 3 (`git grep` over `packages/rest/src`, `packages/runtime/src` and both adapters, tests excluded); the other reader, `endpoint-executor.ts`, is the OpenAPI `object_operation` record id, a different door with a declared parameter. The arity table confirms it: `id` is single-valued on `list` alone. So there is no second door with an `id` filter to extend to, and "both transports" is the seam's full reach.
8. **The order's "the same 400 the repeated `id` gets, #28548's words".** The dev read it as status and code (both 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`) plus #28548's sentence frame, not `repeatedQueryParamMessage`. Right: that message says "supplied N times" and would be false for a key sent once, and the repeated-`id` answer predates #28548 (#7566 / #23214 arity), so "#28548's refusal" can only mean `refuseEmptyListFilter`'s frame, which is what the diff reuses. The pre-existing two-dialect note (the chain's thrown refusal writes the flat `{ error, code }` on REST, the entry arity gate the nested one) was accepted on #28602 and is not moved here.

Claims checked for wrong statements about the surface: the changeset's "Now" message is the literal the builder produces; the PR body's "every adapter hands query keys through unparsed" holds for both Hono adapters read here (the node reference adapter reads `searchParams.getAll`, also unparsed); the body's "no other type reads an `id` spelling" holds per item 7. None found wrong.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28930-bracketed-app-id-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/rest': patch`; line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; a **BREAKING** banner; exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker; Before / Now / Unchanged / Who-sees-it; the remedy as FROM `?id[]=NAME` (or `?id[0]=NAME`) TO `?id=NAME`. The PR title carries `!`, and the PR body carries the same two declaration lines line-initial. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: `(narrowing)` is the BREAKING arm, and a non-protocol change ships `patch` with its banner and ADR-0087 disposition (ruling A, #25105). The level matches what the diff publishes: only `@objectstack/rest` ships the narrowed door; `@objectstack/runtime` moves a test file its package does not ship; `packages/qa/dogfood` is private; nothing under `packages/spec` moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: a query-key spelling on a REST door changes nothing a metadata author writes. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (which runs `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, the ADR-0087 registration gate included) are green on this head.

**The declaration deviation, judged.** The order expected `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; the dev declared `no (narrowing)`. The dev is right. In this repo's one reader of the line (`scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`, `reviewFace`), `yes` is the widening declaration ("a widening in application or UI code, a translation key, a version declaration"), the fourth face is keyed on the exact spelling `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` ("a `Clause-②: no` card that NARROWS a published accept set", ruling record 6203713500), and `yes (narrowing)` is reserved for "a diff that widens AND narrows". This diff widens nothing (① item 6), so a `yes` would have been a false widening declaration; `no (narrowing)` is the same spelling #28602 declared for the same class at the same seam and passed on (record 6555574011). The claim itself wrote "expected ... the dev measures and declares", so the order's line was a prediction, not a ruling. The gate outcome is unchanged either way: both spellings owe this review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the arm, not the value, for breaking-ness. `Skills-docs: none` holds: `git grep` on the head finds no page under `skills/`, `content/docs/` or `apps/docs/` that teaches `meta/app?id`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` in the os-dev-report 6570620675. Nothing to answer.
- **Seam location (premise correction).** The card and the order placed the filter in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`; it lives in `createMetaListAnswer` step 3 of `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, the chain both `meta-collection-routes.ts` and `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` call. Verified at both call sites. The defect reproduced as stated (the card's measurement and the dev's ablation agree on the merge-base's answer). Closed.
- **Evidence: ablation.** Not re-run here (read-only). Read for coherence: the mutation replaced the one call site with `void refuseBracketedAppIdFilter;` so the function stayed declared and the DTS build stayed green, which is a true ablation of the call; the reds reported are exactly the new assertions, three `it.each` rows in the rest unit, the one "reference moves" `it` in parity, the two bracketed `it`s in dogfood; and the census row A staying green under ablation is the correct expectation, since both transports then give the same unfiltered list. Coherent with the diff. Accepted.
- **Evidence: the full dogfood battery.** `(narrowing)` owes it (os-dev.md); reported under the verify lock at this head as 383 files passed, 3 skipped, 3166 tests passed, 28 skipped, no failures. The CI twin, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, is green on this head. Accepted.
- **Evidence: derived gates.** The dev's local record says 64 of 64 families run and green, with two prerequisite re-runs declared. The verdicts of record are the head's check-runs: 54 of 54 completed, 37 success and 17 skipped, none failed, including all eight `Test Core` shards, `Type Check` (four), `Lint` (nine), `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Core`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`. The skipped ones are opt-in harnesses, UI-matrix placeholders and the schedule gate. No merge-base comparison is needed, since nothing is red.
- **Overlap with #28850.** Verified on its file list and patch: its two hunks on `meta-read-doors-live.dogfood.test.ts` are the header comment plus an `ensurePair`/`inPair` import near line 23 and the acceptance[2] `PUT` setup near line 91; this PR appends one `describe` at the end of the top-level block (from line 164) and uses only helpers already in the file (`stack.apiAs`, `codeOf`, `messageOf`, `admin`, `liaison`). Disjoint hunks, no shared symbol; whichever lands second rebases without a conflict. The dev's "no other open PR touches `meta-item-read-gate.ts`, `rest-server.ts`, the rest unit or the parity file" is the dev's reading at report time; the seat's pre-enqueue overlap re-read remains its own.
- **Out of scope: `GET /meta/view?object[]=lead` answers every view (and `package[` is unmeasured).** Judged against the order's ruling, which binds the `id` filter ("whether the same `?id=` filter (or the same query parse) serves other `/meta/:type` list doors; if one seam serves them, they get the same answer; if not, `/meta/app` only and report the others"): the view list's `object` filter is a different key, read by step 4, so the ruling as written does not pull it into this PR, and the dev did what it says, fixed `/meta/app` only and reported the sibling. It is a separate card, not a FAIL of this one. Recorded for that card: it is the same defect class in the same chain, the fix is mechanical (`refuseBracketedAppIdFilter` hard-codes `id`/`app`; a `(param, names, lists)` twin on step 4 serves `object[`), and `package[` is a third site, read at the door entry by `metaItemPackageBinding(req.query?.package)` before the chain on both transports, where an unread key reads as "every package". The seat may instead fold the `object[` arm by claim amendment, as #28548 folded the empty `?object=` (6555101824), at the cost of a patch round and a fresh record on the new head; that is the seat's call, not this record's.
- **Observation, not a finding of the narrowing.** The dogfood control's last assertion, 'a member never sees setup', is vacuous on the showcase stack, which boots no `setup` app for either caller (the dev says so under Acceptance notes); the pruning the card observed came from a full `os dev` boot. The bracketed probes still use `setup` as the order asked and still red on the merge-base (the whole list came back), so the pin's purpose holds; only that one control sentence promises more than the stack can show. Non-blocking.
- `needs:contract-review` is on the PR; this PASS on the current head lets the seat remove it in the same stroke. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published contract: `GetMetaItemsRequestSchema` declares no `id` member, so the spec gives a bracketed `id` no meaning; `?id=` is #7566's transport-level declaration ("narrows to the app of that name"), and no text declares an array spelling; `@objectstack/client`'s `meta.getItems` builds `?package=` only and the console sends no `id` on this read (the producer census PASS record 6555574011 made, unchanged by this diff; `git grep` on the head finds no `id[]` builder outside unrelated UI param widgets). So this is the spec's own refusal class made real, the one #27484 and #28548 ruled for a value that names nothing, not an implementation gap narrowed at the consumer. Attempts to break it: a doubled bracketed key (one answer, ① item 3); a percent-encoded `id%5B%5D` (Hono decodes it to `id[]` before `queries()`); `ids[` and `ID[` (unmatched, consistent with the plain spellings); a dispatcher-only host (same chain, pinned by the census on every type × caller); a non-object query (early return). Nothing breaks.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none that blocks; the vacuous control sentence in ③ may be reworded in the next edit of that file.
